mainTopic: Who went into ים סוף first, and where שבט לוי stood at הר גריזים and הר עיבל
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about who went into ים סוף first. רבי מאיר says שבט בנימין jumped in first, the princes of יהודה threw stones at them, and בנימין was rewarded with the שכינה resting in its portion. רבי יהודה disagrees. In his telling, every tribe refused to go first until נחשון בן עמינדב of יהודה jumped in. פסוקים in תהלים are read as נחשון's prayer from the water, and הקב״ה tells משה to stop praying at length and move the people forward. For this, יהודה earned the kingship. The גמרא then returns to the ברכות and קללות at הר גריזים and הר עיבל and asks where שבט לוי stood. Some say the tribe was split, and רבי says everyone stood below, reading 'על' as 'next to'. Finally, a ברייתא begins explaining general and particular blessings and curses, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שבט בנימין jumped into the sea first
steps.stepSummary: Finishing רבי מאיר's account, שבט בנימין went down into ים סוף first. He supports this with a דרשה on the word רֹדֵם.
steps.simpleTranslation: …שבט בנימין jumped in and went down into the sea first. As the פסוק says, 'There is בנימין, the youngest, רֹדֵם.' Don't read it as רֹדֵם (ruling them). Read it as רָד יָם (went down to the sea).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבי מאיר's story from the previous page. Of all the tribes, שבט בנימין went into the sea first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר brings a פסוק from תהלים as his source. He uses an אל תקרי reading, splitting the word רֹדֵם into two words, רָד יָם, meaning 'went down to the sea.' The same letters now carry a hidden meaning about קריעת ים סוף.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down into the sea first
'Don't read it as…'; a דרשה that reads the same letters a different way

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The opening words, where רבי מאיר says the tribes argued and then בנימין 'jumped in,' are on the previous page.

phrases.english: the tribe of Benjamin
phrases.notes: This sentence began on the previous page. רבי מאיר said the tribes were arguing, and then the tribe of בנימין jumped in.

phrases.english: and went down into the sea first,
as it says: 'There is Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:28

phrases.english: do not read it as 'rodem' (ruling them),
but rather as 'rad yam' (went down to the sea).
phrases.notes: Same letters, just split into two words.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל בִּנְיָמִין וְיָרַד לַיָּם תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי מאיר's account from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, שבט בנימין went into ים סוף first, based on reading רֹדֵם as רָד יָם.

steps.title: The princes of יהודה threw stones at them
steps.stepSummary: The princes of שבט יהודה threw stones at בנימין. This is learned from the next words of the same פסוק, רִגְמָתָם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The princes of יהודה were throwing stones at them. As the פסוק says, 'the princes of יהודה, רִגְמָתָם.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר adds that the princes of יהודה threw stones at בנימין for jumping in first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the rest of the same פסוק. The word רִגְמָתָם sounds like רוֹגְמִים, 'throwing stones.' So one פסוק teaches both facts: who jumped first, and how יהודה reacted.

keyTerms.meaning: The princes of the tribe of יהודה
A word in the פסוק, read here as 'their stoning'

phrases.english: And the princes of Judah were
throwing stones at them,
as it says: 'The princes of Judah, rigmatam.'
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק. רִגְמָתָם sounds like רוֹגְמִים, 'stoning.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail to רבי מאיר's story, drawn from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The princes of יהודה threw stones at בנימין for going in first.

steps.title: בנימין's reward: hosting the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: Because בנימין went in first, it earned the merit of being a 'host' to the שכינה. The source is a פסוק from משה's ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore בנימין הצדיק merited to become a host for the Almighty. As the פסוק says, 'and He rests between his shoulders.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר closes his account with בנימין's reward: the שכינה would rest in its portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לפיכך ('therefore') ties the reward directly to the brave jump into the sea. The פסוק in משה's ברכה to בנימין says ה׳ 'rests between his shoulders,' meaning the שכינה dwells with בנימין.

keyTerms.meaning: A host who welcomes a guest

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's whole story: בנימין jumped first, יהודה threw stones, and בנימין was rewarded with the שכינה resting in its portion.

phrases.english: Therefore the righteous Benjamin merited
and became a host for the Almighty,
as it says: 'and He rests between his shoulders.'
phrases.notes: דברים 33:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reward that follows from בנימין's act in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because it went into the sea first, בנימין merited to host the שכינה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: נחשון of יהודה went in first
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects רבי מאיר's version. In his account no tribe wanted to go first, until נחשון בן עמינדב jumped in, as hinted in a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: That is not how it happened. Rather, one tribe said, 'I'm not going into the sea first,' and another tribe said, 'I'm not going into the sea first.' Then נחשון בן עמינדב jumped in and went down into the sea first. As the פסוק says, 'אפרים surrounds Me with lies, and בית ישראל with deceit, and יהודה still went down with God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר and tells the story a different way. The tribes were not racing to go first. They were all afraid, and נחשון from יהודה was the one who jumped in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things flip here. The tribes were refusing rather than competing, and the hero is יהודה, not בנימין. רבי יהודה reads רָד עִם אֵל in הושע as 'יהודה went down with God,' meaning they went into the water trusting ה׳.
steps.confusionAlert: In רבי מאיר's version the tribes all wanted to go first. In רבי יהודה's version they all refused to go first. Don't mix up the two stories.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the famous idea that נחשון was the first to jump into ים סוף.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: That is not how it happened,
rather, this one said:
I am not going into the sea first,
and that one said:
I am not going into the sea first,
Nachshon son of Amminadav jumped in
and went down into the sea first,
as it says: 'Ephraim surrounds Me with lies,
and the house of Israel with deceit,
and Judah still went down with God.'
phrases.notes: הושע 12:1. רָד עִם אֵל is read here as 'went down with God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's whole account and offers a different one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire story: both who went first and why.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה holds the facts were different. The tribes refused rather than competed, and נחשון of יהודה went first, not בנימין.

steps.title: תהלים records נחשון's prayer in the water
steps.stepSummary: פסוקים in תהלים are read as נחשון's prayer while he stood in the rising water.
steps.simpleTranslation: About him the Writings spell it out: 'Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my soul… I am sunk in the mire of the deep, where there is no standing, etc.' And: 'Let the flood of water not sweep me away, and let the deep not swallow me, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יהודה's story with פסוקים from תהלים. They describe someone sinking in deep water and crying out to ה׳, and here they are read as נחשון's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a picture of the moment itself. The פסוקים speak of water coming 'up to the soul' and of sinking with nowhere to stand. Read as נחשון's words, they show him begging ה׳ to save him from the deep water.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the books of כתובים (such as תהלים)
A flood or current of water

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says בנימין went first. רבי יהודה says נחשון of יהודה went first, and the פסוקים in תהלים are read as his prayer from inside the deep water.

phrases.english: And about him it is spelled out in the Writings:
phrases.notes: קבלה here means כתובים. 'Him' is נחשון.

phrases.english: 'Save me, God,
for the waters have come up to my soul...
phrases.notes: תהלים 69:2-3

phrases.english: I am sunk in the mire of the deep,
where there is no standing, etc.'
'Let the flood of water not sweep me away,
and let the deep not swallow me, etc.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 69:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds פסוקים that fill in רבי יהודה's account of נחשון.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's account that נחשון went into the sea first, before it split.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 69:2-3, 16, read as נחשון's prayer while sinking in the water.

steps.title: משה is told to stop praying and act
steps.stepSummary: While נחשון is in the water, משה prays at length. הקב״ה tells him His beloved ones are drowning and orders him to move the people forward and raise his staff.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time משה was praying at length. הקב״ה said to him: 'My beloved ones are drowning in the sea, and you are praying long before Me?!' משה said: 'Master of the world, what can I do?' He answered: 'Speak to בני ישראל and let them travel forward. And you, lift your staff and stretch out your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רבי יהודה continues. While נחשון is in the water, הקב״ה tells משה to stop his long prayer and take action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before showed נחשון praying from inside the water. Now we see משה praying too, and הקב״ה tells him the moment calls for action. The answer is the פסוק 'speak to בני ישראל and let them travel', which shows the sea will split once the people move forward.

keyTerms.meaning: praying at length, making the prayer long
My beloved ones, meaning בני ישראל

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה הָיָה מֹשֶׁה מַאֲרִיךְ בִּתְפִלָּה,
phrases.english: At that time Moshe was praying at length,
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
My beloved ones are drowning in the sea
and you are praying at length before Me?!
He said before Him: Master of the world!
And what can I do?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִסָּעוּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: 'Speak to the children of Israel, that they travel forward.
And you, lift up your staff
and stretch out your hand, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה הָיָה מֹשֶׁה מַאֲרִיךְ בִּתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's story from נחשון's prayer to משה's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While נחשון was in the water, הקב״ה told משה to stop praying at length and to have the people move forward.

steps.title: יהודה earns the right to rule
steps.stepSummary: Because יהודה went into the sea first, the tribe earned the right to rule over ישראל. The proof is from תהלים: יהודה became His holy one because 'the sea saw and fled'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of this, יהודה earned the right to rule in ישראל. As the פסוק says: 'יהודה became His holy one, ישראל His kingdom.' What is the reason יהודה became His holy one and ישראל His kingdom? Because 'the sea saw and fled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the reward. Because יהודה jumped into the sea first, it became the ruling tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads two פסוקים in תהלים that sit next to each other as cause and effect. 'The sea saw and fled' is the reason that 'יהודה became His holy one.' In other words, the sea split for יהודה's courage, and that is how יהודה earned the kingship. This is the parallel to בנימין's reward in רבי מאיר's version, back in step 3.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה tie a tribe's lasting honor to being first into the sea. For רבי מאיר it was בנימין, who got to host the שכינה. For רבי יהודה it was יהודה, who got the kingship.

phrases.english: Therefore, Yehuda merited
to rule in Israel,
as it says: 'Yehuda became His holy one,
phrases.notes: תהלים 114:2–3

phrases.english: Israel His kingdom.'
What is the reason 'Yehuda became His holy one
and Israel His kingdom'?
Because 'the sea saw and fled.'
phrases.notes: This is the very next פסוק, read as the reason for the one before it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ, זָכָה יְהוּדָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מֶמְשָׁלָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends רבי יהודה's story with the reward for יהודה going in first.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יהודה earned the kingship over ישראל because it went into the sea first and the sea split for it.

steps.title: Was Levi above or below?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב points out a problem. One פסוק puts שבט לוי up on the mountain, and another puts it below with the ארון. So neither answer seems possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, you cannot say לוי stood below, because it already says they were above. And you cannot say they stood above, because it already says they were below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברכות and קללות at הר גריזים and הר עיבל. This step sets up a problem about where שבט לוי stood, and the next step will solve it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דברים, לוי is listed among the tribes standing on הר גריזים, which is 'above'. In יהושע, the לוים stand next to the ארון between the mountains, which is 'below'. Both are written, so the ברייתא shows that each simple answer runs into the other פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
below, between the mountains next to the ארון

steps.confusionAlert: 'Above' and 'below' here are not about heaven and earth. 'Above' means up on the mountain with the other tribes. 'Below' means down in the valley next to the ארון.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
It is impossible to say Levi was below,
since it already says above.
phrases.notes: דברים 27:12 lists לוי among the tribes on הר גריזים.

phrases.english: And it is impossible to say above,
since it already says below.
phrases.notes: יהושע 8:33 has the כהנים and לוים standing by the ארון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר לֵוִי לְמַטָּה, שֶׁכְּבָר נֶאֱמַר לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of the sea and returns to the earlier topic of the ברכות and קללות.
steps.kashyaTarget: Where שבט לוי stood during the ברכות and קללות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים seem to contradict each other: one places לוי on the mountain, the other places it below with the ארון.

steps.title: The tribe was split: elders below
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that שבט לוי was split. The elders of the כהנים and לוים stood below, and the rest of the tribe stood above.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? The elders of the כהנים and the לוים were below, and the rest were above.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא solves the problem from step 8 by saying the tribe stood in two places at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק is talking about a different part of the tribe, so both are true. The senior members of the tribe stood with the ארון below, and everyone else stood with the tribes on הר גריזים.

keyTerms.meaning: the elders of the כהנים and לוים

phrases.english: So how does this work?
The elders of the priesthood and the Levites were below,
and the rest were above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the subject: each פסוק refers to a different part of the tribe.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole tribe had to stand in one place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The elders were below and the rest were above.

steps.title: Another split: those fit to serve below
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה agrees the tribe was split, but divides it differently. Whoever was fit to serve stood below, and the rest stood above.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה says: everyone fit to serve was below, and the rest were above.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives another way to divide שבט לוי between the two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers agree that the tribe was split. They disagree only about who went below. The first answer says the elders went below. רבי יאשיה says it was everyone fit to do the עבודה, so the ones not fit for it stayed on the mountain.

keyTerms.meaning: one who is fit to serve, to do the עבודה

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers solve the contradiction the same way, by splitting שבט לוי. They only argue about who stood with the ארון: the elders, or everyone fit to serve.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya says:
Everyone fit to serve was below,
and the rest were above.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הָרָאוּי לְשָׁרֵת לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way to split the tribe than the answer in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the subject by a different rule: fitness to serve.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those fit to serve were below with the ארון, and the rest were above.

steps.title: רבי says everyone stood below
steps.stepSummary: רבי gives a third view: all the people stood below. They turned toward הר גריזים to open with a blessing, and toward הר עיבל to open with a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Both groups were standing below. They turned their faces toward הר גריזים and opened with a blessing, then toward הר עיבל and opened with a curse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his own answer to where everyone stood. He says nobody was up on the mountains. Everyone stood down below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי יאשיה split שבט לוי between the top of the mountain and the area below. רבי removes the problem completely by putting everyone below. The 'mountain' part is only about which way they faced when they said each blessing or curse.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Gerizim, the mountain of the blessings
Mount Ebal, the mountain of the curses

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
These and those were standing below.
phrases.notes: He means both groups, the לוים and the other tribes, were all down below.

phrases.english: They turned their faces toward Mount Gerizim
and opened with a blessing,
toward Mount Ebal, and opened with a curse.
phrases.notes: The words 'and then they turned' are left out, but that is what he means.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ לְמַטָּה הֵן עוֹמְדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the קשיא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, different from the split-tribe answers in steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: everyone stands below, and 'facing the mountain' replaces 'standing on the mountain'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One פסוק puts some people on the mountain and another puts them below, so the people must be split between the two places.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone stood below and turned to face each mountain in turn.

steps.title: The word 'על' means next to
steps.stepSummary: To fit רבי's view with the פסוק that says the tribes stood 'על הר גריזים', the גמרא explains that 'על' here means 'next to,' not 'on top of.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'on' mean? 'On' means next to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears up a problem with רבי's view. The פסוק seems to say the tribes stood on the mountain, so the גמרא explains the word differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone stood below, the פסוק's word 'על' ('on') looks like it disagrees. The גמרא answers that 'על' can mean 'beside' or 'next to.' So standing 'על הר גריזים' just means standing near it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'על' here as 'on top of.' In this whole section the גמרא reads it as 'right next to.'

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "on"?
phrases.notes: This refers to the פסוק that says the tribes stand 'על הר גריזים' (דברים 27:12).

phrases.english: "On" means next to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי's view from step 11 against the wording of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'על הר גריזים' means physically on top of the mountain, which goes against רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'על' means next to the mountain, so everyone could stand below.

steps.title: Proof that 'על' can mean next to
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי reading 'על' as 'next to' about the frankincense on the rows of bread. The proof is that the curtain screened 'על הארון' even though it was not on top of the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'And you shall put pure frankincense on the row.' רבי says: 'on' means next to. Do you say 'on' means next to, or maybe it only means literally on? When the תורה says 'And you shall screen over the ארון,' you must say 'on' means next to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that reading 'על' as 'next to' is not something new. רבי reads it the same way somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי says the frankincense was placed next to the rows of bread. The ברייתא asks whether 'על' might still mean 'on top,' and answers from the curtain: the תורה says it screens 'על הארון,' but it hung beside the ארון. So 'על' can clearly mean 'next to.'

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
And you shall screen or cover

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:

steps.title: General and particular blessings and curses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about turning toward הר גריזים. It then brings a ברייתא: there is a general and a particular blessing and curse, each tied to learning, teaching, keeping and doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'They turned their faces toward הר גריזים and opened with a blessing, etc.' The חכמים taught: 'Blessed' in general, 'blessed' in particular. 'Cursed' in general, 'cursed' in particular. To learn and to teach, to keep and to do. Thus...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's description of the blessings and curses and starts a new ברייתא about them. The ברייתא is setting up a count that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says each blessing and curse came in two forms. One is general, covering the whole תורה, and one is particular, covering each specific item. Each one is also tied to four actions: learning, teaching, keeping and doing. The word 'הרי' ('thus') shows it is about to add these up.

keyTerms.meaning: In particular, covering one specific item

phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the ברייתא adds everything up.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each blessing and curse has a general form and a particular form, and each is tied to learning, teaching, keeping and doing.
